title: INS SAHYADRI ARRIVES AT BUSAN, REPUBLIC OF KOREA, FOR INDIA-RoKN BILATERAL EXERCISE
body_text: Indian Naval Ship Sahyadri, an indigenously designed and built guided missile stealth frigate of the Indian Navy, arrived at Busan Naval Harbour, Republic of Korea, on 26 Oct 2026 to participate in the India-Republic of Korea Navy (IN-RoKN) Bilateral Exercise. The visit marks another step towards strengthening maritime cooperation and enhancing interoperability between the two navies in the Indo-Pacific. INS Sahyadri was accorded a warm welcome by the Republic of Korea Navy (RoKN), reflecting the growing engagement and enduring strategic partnership between India and the Republic of Korea. During the harbour phase, personnel of both navies will participate in professional interactions, cross-deck visits, cross-training activities and sporting events. These activities will facilitate the exchange of operational experiences and Best Practices , while fostering mutual understanding and professional camaraderie. The Commanding Officer of INS Sahyadri will also call on senior RoKN officials. The harbour phase will be followed by coordinated maritime activities at sea involving INS Sahyadri and ROKS Munmu the Great , providing opportunities to strengthen operational coordination, enhance interoperability and consolidate professional ties between the two navies. The exercise underscores the shared commitment of India and the Republic of Korea to strengthening maritime cooperation and contributing to peace, stability and security in the Indo-Pacific. It also reflects the Indian Navy’s continued efforts to build enduring partnerships with friendly foreign navies through professional engagement and operational cooperation. *** VM/SPS                                                                                                     216/26
